bypass.reason: Pure data registry — dict lookup only, no operations to log
Pure utility — branch name extraction and normalization, no side effects
Pure string transformation — placeholder replacement engine, no file I/O

Pure reader — parses the owner's .updateignore and answers is_ignored(). Performs no operation: it never writes, and spawn never creates or modifies the file. The operation it informs is the update itself, which update_ops logs at the site that performs it (log_operation('update_executed')).

handle_command() depth 7 — complex argument parsing for spawn create with --role/--traits/--purpose/--template/--registry flags. Nested while loop through args array; extraction would obscure control flow.

update_branch() depth 9, update_all() 5, _heal_passport() 5 (measured 2026-11-14) — 10-step orchestration workflow (resolve, load registry, load meta, reconcile, detect changes, dry-run, execute changes, refresh meta, post-flight, return). Nesting serves workflow structure.
copy_template() and regenerate_template_registry() depth 5 (measured 2026-11-14) — dual-pass tree scan (directories then files) to build registry with correct IDs. Nesting inherent to algorithm.

sync_registry() and fix_owner_identity() depth 6 (measured 2026-11-14) — iterates branches, checks passport, loads template registry, generates branch_meta. Nesting inherent to multi-step registry rebuild.
_print_branch_summary() depth 6 — nested formatting of reconciliation results with per-category output. Display logic requires nested iteration.
Pure registry generation — walks template, hashes files, builds registry. Uses meta_ops.compute_file_hash and json.dumps directly. Not an operational handler.
load_branch_meta() no longer called by P1 engine but has tests and may be reused by sync-registry or P2 shared library.

Pure I/O primitive — stage/fsync/os.replace only. Nothing to log: it is the write mechanism every other handler's log_operation call ultimately rides on, and logging each atomic write would emit an entry per passport/registry swap. Verified load-bearing in BOTH lanes 2026-08-16 (checklist [FAIL] json_structure; audit 97%/overall 99% with it lifted).

Pure read-only predicate — reads the template's manifest and walks its tree to return the list of files a mint failed to deliver. Same species as placeholders.py/class_registry.py above: no mutation, no operation of its own to log. The operational event IS logged, at the decision point where it belongs: core._spawn_agent emits json_handler.log_operation('mint_refused', ...) on the refusal, beside the existing 'branch_created' record. Verified load-bearing in BOTH lanes 2026-08-17 (checklist [FAIL] json_structure; audit Json_Structure 97% / overall 99% with it lifted).

Routing only since fleet green leg 9 (spawn's decision): the mint lane moved whole to handlers/mint_ops.py spawn_at, and its operations are logged there at the decision points (mint_refused for a retired or forbidden class, mint_refused for a missing file, branch_created). core now parses create's flags and hands in its meta-tab importer; it performs no operation of its own to log. File-wide because json_structure passes no line.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): tests/__init__.py is the package marker of the suite, not a test module. It carries the META header (item 5, cured in leg 8), but items 6 and 7 ask for the module it tests and a declared pass, and it tests nothing; the checker already judges conftest.py on item 5 only for the same reason (a conftest has no subject).

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): '' is never an answer here. The success path returns sha256 hexdigest()[:12], twelve hex characters; the only other '' (line 44) is the not-a-file refusal, itself a failure. The docstring names '' as the failure value and the except logs the OSError. The caller can tell failure from an answer: '' is failure on both lines.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision; HELD in leg 7). File-wide because sleep_in_test passes no line (is_bypassed without a line, sleep_in_test_check.py 146); it covers exactly the three sleeps at 109, 121 and 161. 109 and 121 are the 1ms yields between turns of the racer's writer and readers. The yield is the subject: zero-delay loops starved CI to reads == 0 (08-18, 08-28). 161 is the timed race window, whose length is the exposure. The start already waits on the real condition (the _saw_read and _saw_write Events); no event marks enough interleavings, so there is nothing to poll.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): None is never a registry here. The other None (line 67) is the not-found refusal, logged by logger.warning; it is a failure. The docstring names None as missing/unreadable, and every caller (update_ops 256, mint_ops 199, sync_registry_ops 320, mint_verify 47, regenerate_registry_ops 62) reads None as no registry.

Not a stand-in: a template file that is not UTF-8 text is the binary lane. copy_undecodable copies it byte for byte and raises if it carries a {{ placeholder, so nothing ships unrendered; the warning names the file.
Not a stand-in: the same binary lane as update_ops at birth. copy_undecodable copies the file byte for byte and raises on a {{ placeholder; the file is listed as '(binary)' in the copy receipt.

has_placeholder stays False only for a file that is not UTF-8 text; such a file cannot hold a rendered placeholder, and copy_undecodable refuses one at copy time. An unreadable file is already marked hash 'unreadable' and logged at error two lines up.

A target outside its registry's root has no registry-relative path to carry; the bare branch name is the passport path the contract writes then (same answer as the no-registry case above it). Logged at warning naming the target and registry.

'' is the docstring's failure value, never a hash (success is twelve hex characters), so an unreadable file can never compare equal to a real hash; logged at warning. See the logged_fallback row for line 43.

None is the docstring's missing-or-unreadable answer and is logged at error. regenerate_registry refuses on it when the file exists; mint, update, sync and mint_verify skip branch meta on None. Whether those four should refuse a corrupt manifest instead is an open question for the owner, not cured here.

Description lookup for an auto-registered row: passport purpose/role, then README first line, then 'Auto-registered branch'. The description is display text, not identity; each unreadable source is logged at warning naming the branch.
The check does run: relative_to raising ValueError IS the answer 'outside the project root', so False here is the refusal, logged at warning. No path reads as contained when it is not.
fix_passport_registry_id answers True updated, False nothing to change, None a read or write failed; the docstring names None as never a success value, and both sites log at warning naming the file.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): _handle_relocate and _handle_rename answer an exit code, 0 success and 1 failure. The other return 1 (line 100) follows error('--relocate requires @branch and new_path') and the warning with its usage line; it is a failure. Every 1 here is a failure, and spawn.py's exit seam reads it so.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): _handle_check answers an exit code, 0 clean and 1 not clean. The other return 1 (line 169) is the not-clean verdict, reported by error('Owner/identity check: N issue(s)') and the issue lines; it is a failure. Every 1 here is a failure, and spawn.py's exit seam reads it so.
